stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO referred to as done; the newly public stock was hit by Friday's tech selloff
stories.quote: It was remarkable to see Anthropic’s IPO plow through the various bits of worrying news that are piling up for the AI industry, with the core thesis of the investing mania very much intact.

facts.text: A broad tech selloff was hitting newly public Anthropic on Friday.
facts.quote: The news added fuel to a broad selloff in tech stocks that was hitting even newly public Anthropic on Friday.

facts.text: Broader markets fell on Thursday while Anthropic rose.
facts.quote: Broader markets took a beating Thursday — it was only Anthropic that soared, and maybe not for long.

facts.text: The issue says the IPO went better than expected, yet people across the AI industry are selling on the news.
facts.quote: It went off better than anyone could have expected. And yet, across the AI industry, a lot of people are selling on the news.

stories.headline: AMD shares fall almost 10% after Hunterbrook short reports on customer financing and China
stories.quote: AMD said the Hunterbrook reports didn’t properly represent its business, but shares fell almost 10% on the news.
stories.description: Number two player in AI chips

facts.text: Hunterbrook's report 'Bank of AMD' says AMD runs an extensive customer-financing-and-investing operation.
facts.quote: features “all of the circular financing of Nvidia, but without the margins or pricing power.”

facts.text: A separate Hunterbrook story says updated chip firmware was delivered to blacklisted Chinese entities.
facts.quote: Hunterbrook said AMD has a China problem too, in the form of updated chip firmware being delivered to multiple blacklisted Chinese entities.

facts.text: AMD's sales to Asian neoclouds serving China's big tech companies are at risk from new US export control rules.
facts.quote: AMD also sells lots of chips to Asian neoclouds that serve China’s big tech companies, and those revenues are at risk from new US government export control rules

stories.headline: Nvidia beats expectations with quarterly sales above $100 billion; stock closes down 3.3% at $146 on Thursday
stories.quote: Nvidia on Tuesday reported earnings that comfortably beat Wall Street expectations, with quarterly sales surpassing $100 billion for the first time.

facts.text: The stock rallied briefly, fell back Wednesday and closed down 3.3% at $146 on Thursday.
facts.quote: The figures were enough to rally the stock briefly, but it fell back Wednesday and closed down 3.3% at $146 Thursday.

facts.text: Board chair Harvey Jones ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO.
facts.quote: New board chair Harvey Jones didn’t sound like a replacement CEO was coming anytime soon and ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO following his forced resignation last week.

facts.text: Interim CEO Colette Kress intends to dial back Nvidia's dealmaking.
facts.quote: The biggest immediate concern in startup land is interim CEO Colette Kress making it clear that she intends to dial back Huang’s aggressive dealmaking.

facts.text: Crunchbase data: Nvidia and NVentures have made a record 121 investments so far in 2026.
facts.quote: Per data from Crunchbase, Nvidia and its venture arm, NVentures, have made a record 121 investments so far in 2026

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's forced resignation as Nvidia CEO last week; three directors reported to favour reinstating him
stories.quote: Chatter about a Huang comeback kicked up again after he said he’d be willing to return as CEO if the board asked, and three directors have privately pushed for him to be reinstated, per Semafor.

facts.text: The resignation happened the week before the issue and was forced.
facts.quote: ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO following his forced resignation last week.

facts.text: The issue considers a comeback unlikely given the allegations.
facts.quote: Yet the gravity of the allegations relating to possible export control violations, to say nothing of affairs with a major customer and employees, makes a comeback unlikely.

facts.text: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner said his Friday letter to the board was not an endorsement of a Huang comeback.
facts.quote: Altimeter’s Brad Gerstner said the letter he sent the board Friday, widely seen as endorsing a Huang comeback, was not that, and he doesn’t want the board to “take shortcuts” in its investigation.

stories.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, ranking at or near the top of model benchmarks
stories.quote: This week it released Gemini 4 Neon, a medium-sized model that had long been in the works. According to the benchmarks, Neon is ranking at or near the top of the most powerful models .

facts.text: Gemini 3.5 Pro was delayed and earlier smaller models trailed rivals.
facts.quote: Gemini 3.5 Pro was delayed and its previous smaller models were not matching up with Anthropic and OpenAI (and even SpaceX).

facts.text: SemiAnalysis had declared Google out of the race.
facts.quote: SemiAnalysis went as far as to flatly declare it cooked and out of the race. “DeepMind is no longer a frontier lab ,” they wrote.

facts.text: Demis Hassabis is referred to as the now former DeepMind leader.
facts.quote: SemiAnalysis was humble about it and (now former) DeepMind leader Demis Hassabis was good natured in response .

stories.headline: Wall Street firms that promised about $500 billion in data centre loans have not yet lent any, per the Wall Street Journal
stories.quote: Big Wall Street investment firms that promised in August to pony up some $500 billion in loans for data centers have yet to dispense a dime, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.

stories.quote: Kalshi faces multiple investigations around whether or not it’s circumventing state gambling laws.
